body.text: IAC transfers heat from the intermediate sodium to the atmosphere.
body.anchor: transfers heat from the intermediate sodium (described in Section 7.1.4) to the atmosphere

body.text: IAC is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions.
body.anchor: is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions

body.text: It also supports start-up and shutdown transitions to and from NSS cooling.
body.anchor: for transition to and from Nuclear Island Salt System cooling

checks.q: When is IAC the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal?
checks.x: IAC is primary and preferred during low power and shutdown.
checks.anchor: is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions

body.text: IAC has two equal capacity trains. Each has an AHX, air stack, air blower, dampers, and air heater in an ASE structure.
body.anchor: consists of two equal capacity trains

body.text: The two ASEs are in the yard on either side of the RAB.
body.anchor: The two ASEs are located in the yard area on either side of the Reactor Auxiliary Building

body.text: An AHX is in series within each intermediate loop. Sodium is on the tube side and air on the shell side.
body.anchor: Intermediate sodium flows on the tube-side of the AHX with airflow on the shell-side

body.text: The ASEs have sodium catch pans and leak detection below the AHXs.
body.anchor: provisions for sodium catch pans and leak detection below the AHXs

body.alt: PSAR Rev 1 figure: IAC Simplified Arrangement

checks.q: Which fluid is on the tube side of the AHX?
checks.x: Intermediate sodium flows on the tube side.
checks.anchor: Intermediate sodium flows on the tube-side of the AHX with airflow on the shell-side

rows.anchor: IAC Active Mode provides normal operation cooling
IAC Blower Mode provides off-normal operation cooling
IAC Passive Mode provides emergency operation cooling

body.text: IAC is shut down and in standby during Mode 1.
body.anchor: The IAC is shut down and available in standby while the plant is operating in Mode-1

body.text: A single train in Active Mode or Blower Mode provides the required heat removal for the limiting decay heat load.
body.anchor: A single train of IAC operating in Blower Mode provides the required heat removal

body.text: In Passive Mode, the limiting decay heat load needs two trains in operation.
body.anchor: with two trains in operation

checks.q: Which IAC mode has natural circulation of sodium and forced airflow?
checks.x: Blower Mode uses natural circulation of sodium and forced airflow.
checks.anchor: IAC Blower Mode provides off-normal operation cooling

checks.q: How many trains are needed in Passive Mode for the limiting decay heat load?
checks.x: Passive Mode provides the required removal with two trains in operation.

body.text: Air dampers above and below the AHXs are normally closed in Mode 1 to limit heat transfer.
body.anchor: are normally closed during Mode-1 operation

body.text: These dampers fail open on loss of power.
body.anchor: The dampers fail open on loss of power

body.text: Blower discharge dampers are normally open and fail open.
body.anchor: The blower discharge dampers are normally open and fail open

body.text: No automatic actuations or manual actions are needed for Passive Mode, and no electrical power is needed to start natural convection airflow.
body.anchor: No electrical power is required to initiate natural convection airflow across the AHX

checks.q: What do the AHX dampers do on loss of power?
o: Close on spring return after a delay
checks.x: The dampers fail open on loss of power.
checks.anchor: The dampers fail open on loss of power

checks.q: Why are the AHX dampers closed in Mode 1?
o: To limit heat transferred from the intermediate sodium
To keep sodium from freezing in the stack
checks.x: They limit heat transferred from the intermediate sodium when IAC is not required.
checks.anchor: to limit heat transferred from the intermediate sodium when the IAC is not required

body.text: IAC parameters are monitored by the NIC, and also by local control panels or local gauges.
body.anchor: are monitored by the Nuclear Island Control System (NIC)

o: NIC and local panels or gauges
checks.x: Parameters are monitored by the NIC and via local panels or gauges.
checks.anchor: are monitored by the Nuclear Island Control System (NIC)

body.text: The ASE diverts leakage to collection points and minimizes the surface area of leaked sodium exposed to air.
body.anchor: by diverting leakage to collection points

body.text: There are no water-based suppression systems and no fire water piping in the ASE.
body.anchor: There are no water-based suppression systems and no fire water piping in the ASE

body.text: Weather caps limit water intrusion into the ASE.
body.anchor: are provided with weather caps to limit water intrusion

checks.q: Why is there no water suppression in the ASE?
o: The AHX contains sodium and contact with water is avoided
checks.x: The IAC is designed to avoid contact between sodium and water.
checks.anchor: the IAC is designed and located to avoid contact between sodium and water

body.text: DL4-HR1 IAC passive mode operation is NSRST. It removes heat when the ISP and RAC are unavailable.
body.anchor: DL4-HR1 IAC Passive Mode Operation

body.text: Passive Mode is the safety-significant defense-in-depth backup to the SR RAC.
body.anchor: provides the safety-significant defense-in-depth backup to the SR Reactor Air Cooling System

body.text: ASE, air stack, AHX, blower, heater, dampers, screens, and stack cap are NSRST.
body.anchor: ASE, Air Stack NSRST SCN1

checks.x: Table 7.2.2-1 lists the AHX as NSRST.

summary.text: IAC has two trains and three modes: Active, Blower, and Passive.
summary.anchor: consists of two equal capacity trains

title: Intermediate Air Cooling System
subject: IAC
intro: IAC is the normal way to reject reactor heat at low power and shutdown. Two trains of air heat exchangers sit in the yard, with three modes from fully powered to fully passive.
